sentences.text: Health visitor Claire Dunmore (S1) confirmed confidentiality of the conversation with the mother, Jade Pritchard (S2), stating that information remains between them and the GP, and
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) confirmed the confidentiality agreement was previously explained by the health visitor.
The visit is for an eight-month review of child Lily, who is approximately eight months old.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that Lily's weaning is progressing well, with porridge in the morning and mashed vegetables at dinner.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that Lily is still on four bottles of milk.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that Lily drinks seven ounces per bottle.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that Lily sometimes does not finish the night bottle.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that Lily is trying finger foods (bits of toast and banana) and gags occasionally, which she finds worrying.
Health visitor Claire Dunmore (S1) stated that gagging is normal and explained the difference between gagging and silent choking.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that Lily sleeps for seven hours and wakes once around three o'clock for a bottle.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her son Mason sleeps worse than Lily.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her mood is generally alright but she feels tired and bored, particularly in the evenings.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) disclosed that she drinks alcohol, specifically a bottle of wine per night, most nights, after the children are in bed.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) confirmed the bottle size is a standard 75 centilitre bottle from the Co-op.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that she smokes weed a couple of nights a week, consuming a joint or two, only when the children are in bed and never in their presence.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that she smokes weed in the garden/out the back door so it is not in the house.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) denied ever using cocaine, stating she has never done it and would not.
Health visitor Claire Dunmore (S1) asked if the mother could drive or deal with a child waking up poorly at 2 am if one of the children did so.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) denied being able to drive or deal with a child waking up poorly, stating she has fallen asleep on the sofa and missed hearing Lily crying.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her son Mason woke her up after she fell asleep on the sofa and told her that Lily was crying.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) expressed uncertainty about how long Lily was crying while the mother was asleep.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her husband Dean works Monday to Friday on lorries and returns on weekends.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that she is the primary carer during the week.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her mother lives on Thornfield Road and helps with Mason on Tuesdays.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her husband Dean works 15 hours a week at Little Acorns.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that her finances are tight, relying on Universal Credit and money sent by her husband Dean.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) reported that electricity costs have increased significantly and they are on a key meter.
Health visitor Claire Dunmore (S1) proposed a referral to the Harbridge Recovery Hub and informing the GP.
Mother Jade Pritchard (S2) agreed to the proposed referral and GP notification.
Health visitor Claire Dunmore (S1) stated she would speak to her safeguarding lead today and would call the mother tomorrow to confirm next steps.
